And on this account the grandees who had made him king repented,
inasmuch as he was not yet mature in intellect and stature.
Now Abbas, one of them, was especially anxious about this,
and he assembled the grandees,
and they went in to al-Mu'tazz's son [Ibn al-Mu'tazz],
and swore {an oath} to him.
And they sent word to al-Muqtadir, and to his mother, and to his nurse, and to his eunuchs,
that they should leave the palace.
Now Mu'nis, the chief of the eunuchs, being filled with zeal,
assembled the rest of the eunuchs and the Turkish slaves.
And they armed themselves and fell suddenly upon the grandees while they were assembled with Ibn al-Mu'tazz,
and they killed Abbas and certain of the grandees,
and the others they imprisoned.
And they brought Ibn al-Mu'tazz himself to the palace,
and at night they strangled him and buried him in that very courtyard.
And thus the kingdom was firmly established for al-Muqtadir.
And in the year 1220
of the Greeks (909 of our Lord?), heavy snow fell in Baghdad,
and it lay on the roofs four fingers deep.
And there was no one at that time in Baghdad
who had ever seen snow in it before.
And after eighteen years,
in the year 315
of the Arabs,
which is the year 1238
of the Greeks, wine vinegar froze in the jugs,
and also eggs,
and also oil flasks,
and the trees withered.
And in that same year (909 of our Lord?), that eunuch Mu'nis entered the territory of the Romans with the army of the Arabs from the pass of Melitene,
and took captives, plundered, and departed.
And in the year 299
of the Arabs, Rustam, the commander of the army of the Arabs, entered the territory of the Romans from the pass of Tarsus,
and captured the fortress of Melias {OCR?} the Armenian,
and burned it.
And in that year,
that al-Muqtadir distributed one hundred thousand gold dinars to the loose women {prostitutes} who were in his palace.
And having emptied his treasuries with extravagances such as these,
and being pressed by the Turkish slaves for their allowances,
and having nothing to give them,
he would torture the scribes and wealthy men with bitter tortures,
and confiscate their property.
For at the beginning of the kingdom of the Arabs,
victory was especially theirs.
And when again the kingdom was extended for them,
